stories.name: Apple stock valuation debate
stories.blurb: Investors and analysts are debating whether Apple's record-high stock price and lofty valuation can keep climbing or are due for a pullback.

stories.name: Apple CEO transition
stories.blurb: John Ternus succeeds Tim Cook as Apple CEO, raising questions about the company's future direction and leadership style.

stories.name: Vanguard Growth ETF Debate
stories.blurb: A recurring theme of financial articles comparing and recommending Vanguard growth-focused ETFs (like VUG and VGT) against rivals as long-term investment options.

stories.name: Apple iPhone Duo launch
stories.blurb: Apple has unveiled its first foldable smartphone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo, marking its most expensive and dramatically redesigned iPhone yet.

stories.name: AI assistant rivalry
stories.blurb: Apple, Meta, and Amazon are competing to dominate AI-powered personal assistants and shopping agents, raising privacy and legal concerns.

stories.name: Apple product launches
stories.blurb: A rolling series of Apple announcements, product releases, and demand signals spanning new iPhones, smart home devices, a leasing program, and expanded U.S. manufacturing.

stories.name: Qualcomm Apple patent deal
stories.blurb: Qualcomm and Apple renewed their long-term global patent licensing agreement, easing investor fears about Qualcomm's revenue but leaving questions about its growth beyond Apple.

stories.name: MP Materials growth
stories.blurb: MP Materials is ramping up rare earth and magnet production, clearing a GM milestone and targeting Apple as its next major customer.

past.name: Index funds trade Apple
past.blurb: Major index ETFs are regularly buying and selling Apple and Nvidia shares as they rebalance their portfolios.

past.name: iPhone 18 demand concerns
past.blurb: Apple is reportedly cutting iPhone 18 Pro component orders and facing analyst warnings of weakening demand, sending its stock lower.

past.name: Iran-Israel Oil Market Swings
past.blurb: Stock markets fluctuate as investors react to escalating and de-escalating US-Iran/Middle East tensions, oil price swings, and their effects on earnings, Fed policy, and economic data.

past.name: Apple Q4 earnings
past.blurb: Apple reported fourth-quarter earnings that beat estimates on strong iPhone sales, though Wall Street remains concerned about the next quarter.

past.name: Meta's Muse AI Surge
past.blurb: Meta's stock rallies as its new AI app Muse gains rapid popularity, boosting investor confidence in the company's AI strategy ahead of Meta Connect.

past.name: TSMC AI chip boom
past.blurb: TSMC's surging AI chip demand and 2nm progress are driving record revenue and lifting Nvidia and other supplier stocks.

past.name: Apple Smart Home Push
past.blurb: Apple is launching a new lineup of smart home devices, led by a $299 HomeView hub with Apple Intelligence and facial recognition, as it challenges Amazon and bets on subscriptions to drive growth.

past.name: Tokenized Stock Trading
past.blurb: Major financial and crypto firms are launching blockchain-based tokens of Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, and other U.S. stocks on Solana and other platforms, enabling 24/7 onchain trading of tokenized equities

past.name: Apple Broadcom chip deal
past.blurb: Apple has signed a multi-year, $30 billion-plus agreement with Broadcom to supply chips through 2031, boosting Broadcom's stock and expanding its Colorado plant.

past.name: Memory Chip Shortage
past.blurb: A global surge in memory and storage chip prices is forcing Apple to raise prices on MacBooks and iPads while even considering banned Chinese chip suppliers to cope with the shortage.

7.text: Apple hit an all-time high and outperformed the Nasdaq while the market and AI stocks sold off. Analysts debate its 37x forward P/E, with DCF models below its ~$349 price, margin guidance of 45–46%, and rising memory costs.

15.text: Apple is developing a secret AI agent, and a job listing revealing these ambitions briefly appeared before being removed. The news affected Meta and Anthropic stock, signaling Apple's intent to compete in AI under John Ternus.

5.text: Apple is barely mentioned; the articles instead compare broad ETFs (VOO, SPY, IVV, QQQM, ONEQ, FQAL, VUG, SFY) on assets, fees, yields, and returns, with tech-heavy funds noted as concentrated. VUG is reported down 18% from its October record.

8.text: Apple plans to launch five devices, creating a timing dilemma for iPhone buyers. Shoppers who wait may get better launch timing rewards.

6.text: OpenAI countersued Apple in California, alleging trade secret theft and that Apple coerced shared suppliers to stall OpenAI's hardware plans, while Apple reportedly develops its own AI agent. Apple also removed MiniMax's Talkie app from the App Store over inappropriate AI messages and child-safety concerns.

18.text: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 12 days after his resignation, sending shares up 30% before the rally faded; Anthropic fell below its IPO price. Apple is not mentioned in these articles.

12.text: Qualcomm is expanding into a fast-growing, supply-limited business while facing weaker handset demand, as Xiaomi’s memory-driven production cuts hurt its phone-chip outlook. The articles compare Qualcomm with Sandisk and barely mention Apple, so they bear on Apple only indirectly through the smartphone market.

22.text: MP Materials is expanding as a domestic magnet supplier, backed by government support and long-term supply agreements with General Motors and Apple. Its earnings call highlighted a growing relationship with a major tech company, implying Apple.

9.text: Iran-Israel tensions are driving oil market swings, with CNBC's pre-market rundown covering resulting business and market updates. Apple is not mentioned; the story bears on Apple only through broader market and energy-price conditions.

14.text: Apple was downgraded to Hold at 37x forward earnings, pricing in 4.9% FY27 EPS growth. Rising memory costs could push Q1 FY27 gross margins down to 45%–46%.

21.text: On Nov. 18, QQQM bought Apple while SPY and SPXL sold it, alongside broad basket trades. IWF's Wednesday activity was led by NVIDIA, with no Apple mention.
